doc.title: Array Class
doc.para: count The count property represents the size of the array.

load The load method loads an array from a file.
Syntax : load(<filename>, <mode=''>)
Loads an array from a text file. Each line of text in the file enters each element, and finally the count property becomes equal to the number of lines in the file. For mode, specify a mode string when reading the file. This depends on the environment in which TJS is running. Specifying a decimal offset following "o" reads from that byte position in the file. Depending on the environment in which TJS is running, this method, the save method, and the saveStruct method cannot be used. The load method returns this Array class object itself.

save The save method writes the array to a file.
Syntax : save(<filename>, <mode=''>)
Writes the array to a file. Each member is output line by line, but references to objects, classes, functions, etc. become empty lines. For mode, specify a mode string when writing the file. This depends on the environment in which TJS is running, but in the case of Kirikiri, specifying "c" applies simple encryption to the file (it can be loaded as is with the load method). Specifying "z" saves the file compressed (cannot be used together with "c"; this can also be loaded as is with the load method). Specifying a decimal offset following "o" writes from that byte position in the file. Specifying "b" saves in binary format (cannot be used together with other mode specifications; this can also be loaded as is with the load method). The save method returns this Array class object itself.

split The split method splits a string.
Syntax : split(<pattern/delimiter_set>, <string>, <(reserved)>, <ignore_empty_elements=false>)
Initializes the array and copies into this array the string split by a pattern or a delimiter set. Specify a pattern or delimiter set for the 1st argument. The pattern must be a regular expression object. For the delimiter set, specify characters that serve as delimiters. By specifying a string, you can specify multiple delimiter characters. The 3rd argument is reserved for future versions. In "ignore empty elements", specify true if empty elements (for example, ,,,,, when using commas as delimiters) should not be copied to the array. Please pay attention to the order of the arguments.

join The join method joins an array into a single string.
Syntax : join(<delimiter>, <(reserved)>, <ignore_empty_elements=false>)
Joins each element of the array with a delimiter and returns the joined string. If "ignore empty elements" is true, void elements in the array are ignored.
var ar = [ "a", "b", void, "d" ]; var s1 = ar.join(","); // "a,b,,d" is assigned to s1 var s2 = ar.join(",",,true); // "a,b,d" is assigned to s2

reverse The reverse method reverses the order of elements in the array.
Syntax : reverse()

saveStruct saveStruct outputs structured data to a file.
Syntax : saveStruct(<filename>, <mode=''>)
The saveStruct method outputs the state of elements to a file in a restorable state. Each element can contain strings, real numbers, octet sequences, and integers. Also, if an element contains an object, only if that object is an instance of the Array class or Dictionary class, the contents of that object are also output to the file. Otherwise, void is output. For example,
([ 1, 2, 3, [4, 5], %[ a : 1, b : 2 ], "string" ]).saveStruct("out.txt");
outputs content such as:
(const) [ 1, 2, 3, (const) [ 4, 5 ], (const) %[ "a" => 1, "b" => 2 ], "string" ]
By evaluating this entire file as a single expression, the same structure as when saved can be restored. Here, (const) indicates that the contents of [ ] or %[ ] consist only of constant terms. When the compiler finds this (const), it can assume that the immediately following in-expression dictionary array or in-expression array consists only of constant terms, and read it with high efficiency. The saveStruct method returns this Array class object itself.

assign The assign method copies an array.
Syntax : assign(<source_array>)
Copies the contents of another array specified in the argument completely.
When a dictionary array (an object of the Dictionary class) is specified as the source array, each member of that dictionary array becomes an array appearing alternately in the order of name and value. The order of members is undefined.

assignStruct The assignStruct method copies an array along with its structure.
Syntax : assignStruct(<source_array>)
Copies the contents of another array specified in the argument completely. Unlike the assign method, if there are arrays or dictionary arrays among the members, their contents are also copied recursively (in the case of the assign method, only references are copied).
clear The clear method deletes all elements of the array.

erase The erase method deletes the element at the specified subscript.
Syntax : erase(<subscript>)
Deletes the subscript at the specified position. Elements after the subscript are shifted forward one by one and packed. If the subscript is out of range, an exception occurs.

remove The remove method deletes elements that have the same value as the specified value.
Syntax : remove(<value>, <remove_all=true>)
Discriminatively compares each element with the specified value (behavior of the === operator) and deletes matching elements. If "remove_all" is false, only the first element found is deleted. Otherwise, all elements found are deleted.

insert The insert method inserts the specified value at the specified position.
Syntax : insert(<position>, <value>)
Inserts the element indicated by value at the subscript position indicated by position. Elements after position are shifted back one by one.

add The add method appends the specified value to the end of the array.
Syntax : add(<value>)
Appends the element indicated by value to the end of the array. This method returns the position where the value was added.

find The find method returns the subscript where the specified value first appears.
Syntax : find(<value>, <search_start_position=0>)
Checks the specified value sequentially starting from the subscript of search start position and returns the subscript where it first appears. Returns -1 when the specified value is not found. Discriminative comparison (behavior of the === operator) is used for comparison.

push The push method appends the specified elements to the end of the array. Unlike the add method, this method returns the size of the array after addition. Also, if multiple arguments are specified, all arguments are added in order.
Syntax : push(<value>, ...)

pop The pop method removes one element from the end of the array and returns it. The removed element is deleted from the array (the array size decreases by one). This method returns the removed element. If there were no elements, it returns void.
Syntax : pop()

unshift The unshift method adds elements to the beginning of the array. When multiple elements are specified, multiple elements can be added to the beginning. In this case, for example, if passed in the order of a, b, c, the elements at the beginning of the array will be in the order of a, b, c. This method returns the size of the array after addition.
Syntax : unshift(<value>, ...)

shift The shift method removes one element from the beginning of the array and returns it. The removed element is deleted from the array (the array size decreases by one). This method returns the removed element. If there were no elements, it returns void.
Syntax : shift()

pack The pack method converts array elements into binary (Octet) according to the string specified in the argument and returns it. The specified string is called a template. A template is a sequence of type specification characters and their lengths. When * is specified as the length, it represents all remaining length. If length is omitted, it is treated as 1.
Syntax : pack(template_string)
The following characters can be used in the template string: a : ASCII string (null character padded) A : ASCII string (space padded) b : Binary string (low bit to high bit order) B : Binary string (high bit to low bit order) c : Signed 1-byte numeric value (-128 to 127) C : Unsigned 1-byte numeric value (0 to 255) d : Double-precision floating point value f : Single-precision floating point value h : Hexadecimal string (low nybble first) H : Hexadecimal string (high nybble first) i : Signed int numeric value (usually 4 bytes) I : Unsigned int numeric value (usually 4 bytes) l : Signed long numeric value (usually 4 bytes) L : Unsigned long numeric value (usually 4 bytes) n : Unsigned short numeric value (network byte order) N : Unsigned long numeric value (network byte order) s : Signed short numeric value (usually 2 bytes) S : Unsigned short numeric value (usually 2 bytes) v : Unsigned short value (little endian) V : Unsigned long value (little endian) x : Null character X : Back up 1 byte @ : Fill with null characters up to an absolute position m : Base64 decode
var oct = array.pack("a4i2");
In this example, 4 characters of the string in element 0 of array are output as char type, and if it is less than 4 characters, \0 is added. After that, the integers from elements 1 to 2 are added as signed 4-byte integers. In other words, it is output as a binary sequence of char * 2 + int * 4.
